Fresh registration preserves the already-parsed simulation terminal order and applies the exact-source-guarded GF180 native model correction. Existing projects and bundled package revisions remain unchanged.

remaining: Complete device-specific geometry, voltage, temperature, reliability and statistical operating envelopes; physical generation/extraction, ESD rating, silicon and RF accuracy remain unqualified.
These 86 entries are catalog symbol views, not 86 distinct independent transistor models. Model-only definitions and alternate selectable models remain separate inventory work.
Named process selections do not imply every device has independent corner data. The public GF180 native model and some SKY130 discrete models reuse fixed source definitions across selections.
SKY130 20 V models contain fixed internal geometry; the two tested instances vary multiplicity, not effective model W/L. Defaults still expose W/L and need an explicit fixed-geometry contract.
Promote the verified explicit capacitor/MOS/isolation packages to new default projects with reproducibility and physical/runtime regression checks.
The 324-case frozen source predates schematic positioning and RF fault additions. The later nine RF cases and 26 focused tests use the updated implementation; earlier raw evidence is not relabelled.
diagnostics: Initial SKY130 core probe sizes lay outside discrete model bins; subsequent test points use explicit supported bins. Original failures are retained.
Initial GF180 reference incorrectly used NMOS drain-silicide spacing for pfet_03v3_dss; corrected from the source symbol before the full sweep.
A helper initially named a nonexistent Python environment; no qualification ran in that attempt.

Initial handoff fixtures overlapped at the same location, then compared binary float spellings exactly. Fixtures now have distinct locations and use the existing 12-significant-digit export precision contract.
Linux focused tests initially lacked two repository example directories. Including the actual fixtures resolves the failure; no production assertion is skipped.
